当一个或两个操作数都是实数（`float`或`double`）时，结果是一个实数。

resolved.title: 运算符优先级

content.text:
C语言根据运算符的**优先级**来计算算术表达式。

`+`和`-`的优先级相同，`*`、`/`和`%`的优先级也相同。

首先按照从左到右的顺序执行`*`、`/`和`%`，然后是`+`和`-`。
你可以通过使用圆括号`()`来改变计算的顺序，表示哪些运算要先执行。

例如，`5+3*2`的结果是11，而`(5+3)*2`的结果是16。

**例如：**
content.text_html:
C evaluates a numeric expression based on operator precedence. The + and – are equal in precedence, as are *, /, and %. The *, /, and % are performed first in order from left to right and then + and -, also in order from left to right. You can change the order of operations by using parentheses ( ) to indicate which operations are to be performed first. For example, the result of 5 + 3 * 2 is 11, where the result of (5 + 3) * 2 is 16.

For example:

C语言根据**运算符的优先级来评估数字表达式。 +和-的优先级相同，、/和%的优先级也相同。 首先按照从左到右的顺序执行、/和%，然后是+和-，也是按照从左到右的顺序。 你可以通过使用圆括号（ ）来改变操作的顺序，表示哪些操作要先执行。 例如，5+32的结果是11，而（5+3）2的结果是16。

content.text: C在执行计算算术表达式时，对于顺序无关的运算可能不是严格的从左到右计算。例如，`x*y*z`可能被视为`(x * y) * z` 或`x * (y * z)`。如果顺序很重要，请将表达式分成不同的语句。
content.text_html:
C may not evaluate a numeric expression as desired when the associative property allows any order. For example, xyz may be evaluated as (x * y) * z or as x * (y * z). If order is important, break the expression into separate statements.

当关联属性允许任何顺序时，C可能不会如愿地评估一个数字表达式。例如，xyz可能被评估为（xy）z或x（yz）。如果顺序很重要，请将表达式分成不同的语句。

resolved.title: 赋值运算符
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Assignment Operators[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

An [b]assignment statement[/b] evaluates the expression on the right side of the equal sign first and then assigns that value to the variable on the left side of the =. This makes it possible to use the same variable on both sides of an assignment statement, which is frequently done in programming.
[b][/b][s0l0!-header][b]For example[/b]:[/s0l0!-header] [code format="c" ]int x = 3;
x = x + 1;  /* x is now 4 */[/code]
To shorten this type of assignment statement, C offers the += [b]assignment operator[/b]. The statement above can be written as [code format="c" ]x += 1;  /* x = x + 1 */[/code]
Many C operators have a corresponding assignment operator. The program below demonstrates the arithmetic assignment operators: [code format="c" codeId="1630"]int x = 2;

x += 1;  // 3
x -= 1;  // 2
x *= 3;  // 6
x /= 2;  // 3
x %= 2;  // 1
x += 3 * 2;  // 7[/code]
Look carefully at the last assignment statement. The entire expression on the right is evaluated and then added to x before being assigned to x. You can think of the statement as x = x + (3 * 2).
[note]Run the code and see how it works![/note]

resolved.title: 自增及自减运算
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Increment & Decrement[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

Adding 1 to a variable can be done with the [b]increment operator[/b] ++. Similarly, the [b]decrement operator[/b] -- is used to subtract 1 from a variable.
[b][/b][s0l0!-header][b]For example[/b]:[/s0l0!-header] [code format="c" ]z--;  /* decrement z by 1 */
y++; /* increment y by 1 */[/code]
The increment and decrement operators can be used either [b]prefix[/b] (before the variable name) or [b]postfix[/b] (after the variable name). Which way you use the operator can be important in an assignment statement, as in the following example. [code format="c" codeId="1637"]z = 3;
x = z--;  /* assign 3 to x, then decrement z to 2 */
y = 3;
x = ++y;  /* increment y to 4, then assign 4 to x */[/code]
The [b]prefix [/b]form increments/decrements the variable and then uses it in the assignment statement.
The [b]postfix [/b]form uses the value of the variable first, before incrementing/decrementing it.
[note]Run the code and see how it works![/note]
